controls.label: Query matrix Q
controls.help: Sets the query rows. Changing Q changes Raw dot products QK^T, Scaled scores S, Attention weights A, Row sums of A and Attention output O; it never changes Scale factor c.

controls.label: Key matrix K
controls.help: Sets the key rows that queries are compared against. Changing K changes Raw dot products QK^T, Scaled scores S, Attention weights A, Row sums of A and Attention output O; it never changes Scale factor c.

controls.label: Value matrix V
controls.help: Sets the value rows that get averaged. Changing V leaves Raw dot products QK^T, Scale factor c, Scaled scores S, Attention weights A and Row sums of A untouched, and changes only Attention output O.

controls.label: Key dimension dk
controls.help: Sets the key dimension used in the scaling factor. Changing dk changes Scale factor c, Scaled scores S, Attention weights A, Row sums of A and Attention output O, but not Raw dot products QK^T.

controls.label: Apply 1/sqrt(dk) scaling
controls.help: Turns the division by sqrt(dk) on or off. It changes Scale factor c, Scaled scores S, Attention weights A, Row sums of A and Attention output O, but not Raw dot products QK^T.

explorations.title: Tied scores give uniform weights
explorations.instruction: Predict: when both keys give a query the same score, will the attention weights be peaked or spread evenly? Then apply the preset, which sets Query matrix Q, Key matrix K, Value matrix V and Key dimension dk.
explorations.observe: Scaled scores S becomes [[0.7071, 0.7071], [0.7071, 0.7071]], Attention weights A becomes [[0.5, 0.5], [0.5, 0.5]], Row sums of A stays [1, 1], and Attention output O becomes [[2, 3], [2, 3]], the plain average of the two value rows.
explorations.why: Softmax exponentiates the scores and divides by their total; equal scores give equal exponentials, so every weight is one half. Multiplying both tied scores by the same Scale factor c keeps the tie, so scaling changes the numbers in Scaled scores S but not the weights.

explorations.title: A dominant score sharpens when scaling is off
explorations.instruction: Predict: for the same Q and K, does turning the scaling toggle off make the weights more peaked or flatter? Then apply the preset, which sets Query matrix Q, Key matrix K, Value matrix V, Key dimension dk and Apply 1/sqrt(dk) scaling.
explorations.observe: Scale factor c reads 1, so Scaled scores S equals Raw dot products QK^T at [[4, 0], [0, 4]]. Attention weights A becomes [[0.9820, 0.0180], [0.0180, 0.9820]], Row sums of A stays [1, 1], and Attention output O becomes [[1.0360, 2.0360], [2.9640, 3.9640]], pulled toward the dominant value row of each query.
explorations.why: Dropping the 1/sqrt(dk) division widens the gap between the winning score and the losing score, and softmax amplifies gaps exponentially, so the large weight grows and the output moves closer to the dominant value row. The row sum stays one because softmax always divides by the total of the exponentials.

tests.name: tied scores give uniform weights and the average of the value rows
scale factor is one over the square root of the key dimension
scaling off leaves the scores unscaled and softmax over two scores

invariants.name: every row of the attention weights sums to one
the reported row sums add up to the number of queries
attention weights stay inside the unit interval
the scale factor stays between one quarter and one
